==Events==
===Pre-1600===
*[[1477]] &ndash; [[Battle of Nancy]]: [[Charles the Bold]] is defeated and killed in a conflict with [[René II, Duke of Lorraine]]; [[Duchy of Burgundy|Burgundy]] subsequently becomes part of France.<ref>{{cite book|title=A guide to the town of Berne, by a Cantab|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q8IAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA5|year=1859|page=5}}</ref>

===1601–1900===
*[[1675]] &ndash; [[Battle of Turckheim|Battle of Colmar]]: The French army defeats forces from Austria and [[Brandenburg]].<ref>{{cite book|author=William Edwards|title=Notes on European History: The reformation and ascendancy of France, 1494-1715|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QAILAQAAMAAJ|year=1952|publisher=Rivingtons|page=530}}</ref>
*[[1757]] &ndash; [[Louis XV]] of France survives an [[assassination]] attempt by [[Robert-François Damiens]], who becomes the last person to be [[Capital punishment|executed]] in France by [[Hanged, drawn and quartered|drawing and quartering]] (the traditional form of capital punishment used for [[regicide]]s).<ref>{{cite EB1911 |wstitle=Damiens, Robert François |volume=7 |page=788}}</ref>
*[[1781]] &ndash; [[American Revolutionary War]]: [[Richmond, Virginia]], is [[Raid on Richmond|burned]] by [[Kingdom of Great Britain|British]] [[Her Majesty's Naval Service|naval forces]] led by former American general [[Benedict Arnold]].<ref>{{Cite EB1911|wstitle= Arnold, Benedict |volume= 02 | pages = 633–634; see page 634 |quote= ...and was employed in leading an expedition into Virginia which burned Richmond...}}</ref>
*[[1822]] &ndash; The government of [[Central America]] votes for [[Central America under Mexican rule|total annexation]] to the [[First Mexican Empire]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kenyon|first1=Gordon|date=1 May 1961|title=Mexican Influence in Central America, 1821–1823|journal=Hispanic American Historical Review|publisher=[[Duke University Press]]|volume=41|issue=2|doi=10.1215/00182168-41.2.175|doi-access=|jstor=2510200|url=https://read.dukeupress.edu/hahr/article/41/2/175/160110/Mexican-Influence-in-Central-America-1821-1823|access-date=3 July 2022|pages=183–184|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
*[[1875]] &ndash; The [[Palais Garnier]], one of the most famous [[opera house]]s in the world, is inaugurated in Paris.<ref>{{cite book|author=Anthony Gishford|title=Grand opera: the story of the world's leading opera houses and personalities|url=https://archive.org/details/grandoperastoryo00gish|url-access=registration|date=November 1972|publisher=Viking Press|page=[https://archive.org/details/grandoperastoryo00gish/page/55 55]|isbn=978-0-670-34749-0}}</ref>
*[[1895]] &ndash; [[Dreyfus affair]]: French army officer [[Alfred Dreyfus]] is stripped of his rank and sentenced to life imprisonment on [[Devil's Island]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Brian Lenihan|title=For the record|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1KsMAQAAMAAJ|year=1991|publisher=Blackwater Press|isbn=978-0-86121-362-7|page=4}}</ref>
*[[1900]] &ndash; Irish nationalist leader [[John Edward Redmond]] calls for revolt against British rule.<ref>{{cite book|first=Jacques|last=Legrand|title=Chronicle of the 20th Century|publisher=Ecam Publication|year=1987|page=10|isbn=0-942191-01-3}}</ref>

===1901–present===
*[[1911]] &ndash; [[Kappa Alpha Psi]], the world's third-oldest and largest [[black fraternity]], is founded at [[Indiana University]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Journal of the House of Representatives of the State of Michigan|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VUTiAAAAMAAJ|year=1985|publisher=Morse & Bagg|page=2731}}</ref>
*[[1912]] &ndash; The sixth All-Russian Conference of the [[Russian Social Democratic Labour Party]] ([[Prague Party Conference]]) opens. In the course of the conference, [[Vladimir Lenin]] and his supporters break from the rest of the party to form the [[Bolshevik]] movement.<ref>{{cite book|author=Vladimir Ilʹich Lenin|title=Collected Works|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cY4fAQAAMAAJ|year=1971|publisher=Progress Publishers|page=536}}</ref>
*[[1913]] &ndash; [[First Balkan War]]: The [[Battle of Lemnos (1913)|Battle of Lemnos]] begins; Greek admiral [[Pavlos Kountouriotis]] forces the Turkish fleet to retreat to its base within the [[Dardanelles]], from which it did not venture for the rest of the war.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Richard Arnold-Baker|author2=George P. Cremos|title=Averof: The Ship that Changed History|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EZffAAAAMAAJ|year=1990|publisher=Akritas Publications|isbn=978-960-7006-32-5|page=30}}</ref>
*[[1914]] &ndash; The [[Ford Motor Company]] announces an [[Eight-hour day|eight-hour workday]] and minimum daily wage of $5 in salary plus bonuses.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://learning.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/01/05/jan-5-1914-henry-ford-implements-5-a-day-wage/ |title=Henry Ford implements $5-a-day wage |date=5 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105070053/https://learning.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/01/05/jan-5-1914-henry-ford-implements-5-a-day-wage/ |archive-date=2018-01-05 |url-status=live|access-date=4 January 2018}}</ref>
*[[1919]] &ndash; The [[German Workers' Party]], which would become the [[Nazi Party]], is founded in [[Munich]].<ref>{{cite book|author=F. L. Carsten|title=The Rise of Fascism, Second Edition|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=97gy4DHuY9EC&pg=PA91|date=13 November 1982|publisher=University of California Press|isbn=978-0-520-04643-6|page=91}}</ref>
*[[1925]] &ndash; [[Nellie Tayloe Ross]] of [[Wyoming]] becomes the first female governor in the United States.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Historical Encyclopedia of Wyoming|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rV48AAAAIAAJ|year=1970|publisher=Wyoming Historical Institute|page=237}}</ref>
*[[1933]] &ndash; Construction of the [[Golden Gate Bridge]] begins in [[San Francisco Bay]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lib.berkeley.edu/news_events/bridge/gate_2.html |title=Bridging the Bay: Bridges That Never Were |publisher=UC Berkeley Library |access-date=February 19, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110522104530/http://www.lib.berkeley.edu/news_events/bridge/gate_2.html |archive-date=May 22, 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*[[1941]] &ndash; [[Amy Johnson]], a 37-year-old pilot and the first woman to fly solo from London to Australia, disappears after bailing out of her plane over the River Thames, and is presumed dead.<ref>{{cite book|title=Amy Johnson: queen of the air|last=Gillies|first= Midge|date=2004|publisher=Phoenix|isbn=0-7538-1770-5|location=London|oclc=56451512}}</ref> 
*[[1944]] &ndash; The ''[[Daily Mail]]'' becomes the first major [[London]] newspaper to be published on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean.<ref>{{cite book|author=Joseph Nathan Kane|title=Famous First Facts and Records|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NttiC-UaOTMC|page=416}}</ref>
*[[1945]] &ndash; The [[Soviet Union]] recognizes the new pro-Soviet [[Provisional Government of the Republic of Poland]].<ref>{{cite book|author1=Geoffrey Swain|author2=Nigel Swain|title=Eastern Europe Since 1945|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RHU7DwAAQBAJ&pg=PA33|date=23 November 2017|publisher=Macmillan International Higher Education|isbn=978-1-137-60513-9|page=33}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
*[[1948]] &ndash; The [[Semiramis Hotel bombing]] kills at least 23 people.<ref name="L&C">{{Cite book |last1=Lapierre |first1=Dominique |title=O Jerusalem |last2=Collins |first2=Larry |year=1972 |pages=128–133}}</ref>
*[[1949]] &ndash; In his State of the Union address, United States President [[Harry S. Truman]] unveils his [[Fair Deal]] program.<ref>{{cite book|author=Melvyn P. Leffler|title=A Preponderance of Power: National Security, the Truman Administration, and the Cold War|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pIIeG_yn72wC&pg=PA266|year=1992|publisher=Stanford University Press|isbn=978-0-8047-2218-6|page=266}}</ref>
*[[1953]] &ndash; The play ''[[Waiting for Godot]]'' by [[Samuel Beckett]] receives its première in Paris.<ref>{{cite book|author=Alan Astro|title=Understanding Samuel Beckett|url=https://archive.org/details/understandingsam0000astr|url-access=registration|year=1990|publisher=Univ of South Carolina Press|isbn=978-0-87249-686-6|pages=[https://archive.org/details/understandingsam0000astr/page/16 16]}}</ref>
*[[1957]] &ndash; In a speech given to the [[United States Congress]], United States President [[Dwight D. Eisenhower]] announces the establishment of what will later be called the [[Eisenhower Doctrine]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Heiko Meiertöns|title=The Doctrines of US Security Policy: An Evaluation under International Law|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-ZQrT7il4NcC&pg=PA122|date=10 June 2010|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-1-139-48913-3|page=122}}</ref>
*[[1967]] &ndash; [[Cultural Revolution]]: The [[Shanghai People's Commune]] is established following the [[Seizure of power (Cultural Revolution)|seizure of power]] from local city officials by revolutionaries.<ref>{{cite book|last=Meisner|first=Maurice|author-link=Maurice Meisner|title=Mao's China and After: A History of the People's Republic|year=1986|location=[[New York City|New York]]|publisher=[[Free Press (publisher)|Free Press]]|isbn=978-0-02-920870-0|oclc=13270932|edition=3rd|url=https://libcom.org/library/maos-china-after-history-peoples-republic-maurice-meisner|pages=327–329}}</ref>
*[[1968]] &ndash; [[Alexander Dubček]] comes to power in [[Czechoslovakia]], effectively beginning the "[[Prague Spring]]".<ref>{{cite book|author=Karen Dawisha|title=The Kremlin and the Prague Spring|url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_FNxU19KzoKIC|date=1 January 1984|publisher=University of California Press|isbn=978-0-520-04971-0|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_FNxU19KzoKIC/page/n29 17]}}</ref>
*[[1969]] &ndash; The [[Venera 5]] space probe is launched at 06:28:08 UTC<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1969-001A|title=NASA – NSSDCA – Spacecraft – Details|website=nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov|access-date=2019-11-13|archive-date=2019-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514144545/https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1969-001A|url-status=dead}}</ref> from [[Baikonur Cosmodrome|Baikonur]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.astronautix.com/craft/ven2vv69.htm|title=Venera 2V (V-69)|date=2012-04-05|access-date=2019-11-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405003320/http://www.astronautix.com/craft/ven2vv69.htm|archive-date=2012-04-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/archives/from-the-archives-may-17-1969-soviet-spacecraft-lands-on-venus/article27152921.ece|title=From the Archives (May 17, 1969): Soviet spacecraft lands on Venus|date=2019-05-17|work=The Hindu|access-date=2019-11-13|issn=0971-751X}}</ref>
*  1969 &ndash; [[Ariana Afghan Airlines Flight 701]] crashes in [[Fernhill, West Sussex]], UK, while on approach to [[Gatwick Airport]], killing 50 people.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ranter|first=Harro|title=ASN Aircraft accident Boeing 727-113C YA-FAR London-Gatwick Airport (LGW)|url=https://aviation-safety.net/database/record.php?id=19690105-0|access-date=2022-01-05|website=aviation-safety.net|publisher=[[Aviation Safety Network]]}}</ref>
*[[1970]] &ndash; The 7.1 {{M|w}} [[1970 Tonghai earthquake|Tonghai earthquake]] shakes [[Tonghai County]], [[Yunnan]] province, China, with a maximum [[Mercalli intensity scale|Mercalli intensity]] of X (''Extreme''). Between 10,000 and 15,000 people are known to have been killed and about another 26,000 are injured.<ref>{{cite book| ref=Reference-Zchau-2003 |last=Zschau|first=Jochen|author2=Andreas N. Küppers|title=Early Warning Systems for Natural Disaster Reduction|year=2003|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-540-67962-2|page=482}}</ref>
*1970 &ndash; A [[Spantax]] [[Convair 990 Coronado|Convair CV-990 Coronado]] [[1970 Stockholm Spantax Convair CV-990 crash|crashes]] during takeoff from [[Stockholm Arlanda Airport]], killing five people.<ref name="AS.net">{{cite web |title=05 JAN 1970 |url=http://aviation-safety.net/database/record.php?id=19700105-1 |access-date=13 January 2012 |website=Aviation Safety Network |publisher=[[Flight Safety Foundation]]}}</ref>
*[[1972]] &ndash; US President [[Richard Nixon]] announces the [[Space Shuttle program]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Space Shuttle Program Fast Facts|url=https://www.cnn.com/2013/10/21/us/space-shuttle-program-fast-facts/index.html|access-date=2022-01-13|publisher=CNN|date=21 October 2013}}</ref> 
*[[1975]] &ndash; The [[Tasman Bridge]] in [[Tasmania]], Australia, [[Tasman Bridge disaster|is struck]] by the bulk ore carrier ''Lake Illawarra'', killing twelve people.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Acts of the Parliament of Tasmania|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4eI_AQAAIAAJ|year=1975|publisher=Government Printer|page=68}}</ref>
*[[1976]] &ndash; The [[Khmer Rouge]] announce that the new Constitution of [[Democratic Kampuchea]] is ratified.<ref>{{cite book|last=Nhem|first=Boraden|title=The Khmer Rouge: Ideology, Militarism, and the Revolution That Consumed a Generation|location=Santa Barbara, Calif.|publisher=Praeger|date=2013|isbn=978-0-313-39337-2|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZRiMAQAAQBAJ|page=45}}</ref>
*  1976 &ndash; [[The Troubles]]: Gunmen [[Kingsmill massacre|shoot dead ten Protestant civilians]] after stopping their minibus at Kingsmill in [[County Armagh]], Northern Ireland, UK, allegedly as retaliation for a string of attacks on [[Irish Catholic]] civilians in the area by [[Ulster loyalism|Loyalists]], particularly the [[Reavey and O'Dowd killings|killing of six Catholics the night before]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Darach MacDonald|title=The Chosen Fews: Exploding Myths in South Armagh|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WIMiAQAAIAAJ|year=2000|publisher=Mercier Press|isbn=978-1-85635-329-8|page=181}}</ref>
*[[1991]] &ndash; [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] forces enter [[Tskhinvali]], the capital of [[South Ossetia|South Ossetia, Georgia]], opening the [[South Ossetia war (1991–1992)|1991–92 South Ossetia War]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Zürcher|first=Cristopher|author2=[[Pavel Baev]], Jan Koehler|title=Understanding civil war: evidence and analysis, Volume 2|publisher=The World Bank|year=2005|chapter=Civil Wars in the Caucasus|isbn=978-0-8213-6049-1|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yNTQ-BDLPxIC&q=south+ossetia| access-date= 21 July 2010 <!--DASHBot-->}}</ref>
*  1991 &ndash; [[Somali Civil War]]: The [[Embassy of the United States, Mogadishu|United States Embassy to Somalia]] in [[Mogadishu]] is [[Operation Eastern Exit|evacuated by helicopter airlift]] days after the outbreak of violence in Mogadishu.<ref>{{cite book|author=Leo J. Daugherty III|title=The Marine Corps and the State Department: Enduring Partners in United States Foreign Policy, 1798-2007|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ir-hm6IGWnEC&pg=PA284|date=22 April 2009|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-0-7864-5301-6|page=284}}</ref>
*[[1993]] &ndash; The oil tanker [[MV Braer|MV ''Braer'']] runs aground on the coast of the [[Shetland]] Islands, spilling 84,700 tons of crude oil.<ref>{{csr|register=PSIX|id=VN83930947|shipname=Braer|access-date=2008-04-21}}</ref>
*[[2003]] &ndash; A [[Tel Aviv central bus station massacre|suicide bombing]] at the [[Tel Aviv central bus station]] kills 23 people and injures over 100 more.
*[[2005]] &ndash; The [[Eris (dwarf planet)|dwarf planet Eris]] is discovered by [[Palomar Observatory]]-based astronomers, later motivating the [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU) to [[definition of planet|define the term ''planet'']] for the first time.<ref name="New Planet">{{cite web| title = The discovery of 2003 UB313 Eris, the largest known dwarf planet|url=http://www.gps.caltech.edu/~mbrown/planetlila/| last = Brown| first = Mike| publisher = California Institute of Technology, Department of Geological Sciences|year = 2006| access-date = May 3, 2007| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719163702/http://www.gps.caltech.edu/~mbrown/planetlila/| archive-date = July 19, 2011| url-status = live}}</ref>
*[[2014]] &ndash; A launch of the communication satellite [[GSAT-14]] aboard the [[Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle|GSLV MK.II D5]] marks the first successful flight of an [[CE-7.5|Indian cryogenic engine]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.isro.gov.in/gslv-d5/mission.aspx | title=GSLV-D5 with Indigenous Cryogenic Stage successfully launches GSAT-14 from SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota on 5 January 2014 | publisher=ISRO | date=5 January 2014 | access-date=5 January 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104230506/http://www.isro.gov.in/gslv-d5/mission.aspx | archive-date=4 January 2014 }}</ref>
*[[2022]] &ndash; Kazakh President [[Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] dismisses Prime Minister [[Asqar Mamin]] and declares [[state of emergency]] over the [[2022 Kazakh unrest]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-05 |title=Kazakh president sacks cabinet, declares emergency amid unrest |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/1/5/emergency-declared-in-kazakhstans-almaty-mangistau-amid-unrest |access-date=2023-08-17 |publisher=Al Jazeera}}</ref>
*[[2023]] &ndash; The [[2023 Sinaloa unrest]] begins.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 January 2023 |title=Mexican airline Aeromexico says a plane was hit by gunfire, no reported injuries |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/mexican-airline-aeromexico-says-plane-was-hit-gunfire-no-reported-inju-rcna64520 |access-date=5 January 2023 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref>
*[[2024]] &ndash; [[Alaska Airlines Flight 1282]] makes an emergency landing at [[Portland International Airport]] after a door plug blows off the Boeing 737 MAX 9 operating the flight. There are no fatalities, but the accident prompts the [[Boeing 737 MAX|737 MAX to be grounded]] and renews scrutiny on [[Boeing manufacturing and design issues|Boeing's manufacturing and design issues]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=January 12, 2024 |title=FAA Increasing Oversight of Boeing Production and Manufacturing |url=https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-increasing-oversight-boeing-production-and-manufacturing |access-date=January 12, 2024 |website=Federal Aviation Administration}}</ref>

==Births==
===Pre-1600===
*[[1209]] &ndash; [[Richard of Cornwall|Richard, 1st Earl of Cornwall]], English prince, nominal King of Germany (died 1272)<ref>{{cite book | first=Frederick Lewis | last=Weis| editor-first1 = Walter Lee | editor-last1 = Sheppard | editor-first2 = David | editor-last2 = Faris | title=Ancestral Roots of Certain American Colonists who Came to America Before 1700: The Lineage of Alfred the Great, Charlemagne, Malcolm of Scotland, Robert the Strong, and Some of Their Descendants | location=London, U.K. | publisher=Genealogical Publishing Com | year=1992 |page=232| isbn = 978-0-8063-1367-2}}</ref>
*[[1530]] &ndash; [[Gaspar de Bono]], monk of the Order of the Minims (died 1571)<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aMx5C4BtFwAC&q=%22gaspar+de+bono%22|first1=Pietro Agostino |last1=Miloni|title=Vida del beato Gaspar de Bono ... del orden de Minimos|place=Valencia|translator-first=Francisco |translator-last=Burguete|year=1787|access-date=2019-09-11}}{{in lang|es}}</ref>
*[[1548]] &ndash; [[Francisco Suárez]], Spanish priest, philosopher, and theologian (died 1617)<ref>{{cite book|author1=Francisco Suárez|author2=Henry Davis|title=Selections from Three Works of Francisco Suárez, S.J.: The photographic reproduction of the selections from the original editions|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vS6iAAAAMAAJ|year=1944|publisher=Clarendon Press|page=xxxvii}}</ref>
*[[1587]] &ndash; [[Xu Xiake]], Chinese geographer and explorer (died 1641)<ref>{{cite book|author1=Chun-shu Chang|author2=Shelley Hsueh-lun Chang|title=Crisis and Transformation in Seventeenth-century China: Society, Culture, and Modernity in Li Yü's World|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UuXmRrr6F0MC&pg=PA314|year=1998|publisher=University of Michigan Press|isbn=0-472-08528-X|page=314}}</ref>
*[[1592]] &ndash; [[Shah Jahan]], Mughal emperor (died 1666)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Shah-Jahan|title=Shah Jahān|website=Encyclopædia Britannica|access-date=16 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814105459/https://www.britannica.com/biography/Shah-Jahan|archive-date=14 August 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

===1601–1900===
*[[1620]] &ndash; [[Miklós Zrínyi]], Croatian military commander (died 1664)<ref>{{Cite EB1911|wstitle= Zrinyi, Miklós, Count (younger) |volume= 28 |last= Bain |first= Robert Nisbet |author-link= Robert Nisbet Bain | pages = 1045&ndash;1046 }}</ref>
*[[1640]] &ndash; [[Paolo Lorenzani]], Italian composer (died 1713)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/paolo-lorenzani_(Dizionario-Biografico)|title=Lorenzani, Paolo|website=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani|publisher=Treccani|language=it|access-date=16 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181202024642/http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/paolo-lorenzani_(Dizionario-Biografico)/|archive-date=2 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>
*[[1735]] &ndash; [[Claude Martin]], French-English general and explorer (died 1800)<ref>{{cite book|author1=M. A. Beg|author2=M.A.J. Beg|title=Guide to Lucknow|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QPzf4TxgKTcC&pg=PA54|date=July 2002|publisher=Asian Educational Services|isbn=978-81-206-1536-6|page=54}}</ref>
*[[1767]] &ndash; [[Jean-Baptiste Say]], French economist and academic (died 1832)<ref>{{cite book|author=Evelyn L. Forget|title=The Social Economics of Jean-Baptiste Say: Markets and Virtue|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vpGEAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA12|date=31 January 2002|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-134-63080-6|page=12}}</ref>
*[[1779]] &ndash; [[Stephen Decatur]], American commander (died 1820)<ref>{{cite book|author=Benson John Lossing|title=The Pictorial Field-book of the War of 1812|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=itN2AAAAMAAJ&pg=PA989|year=1869|publisher=Harper & Brothers|pages=989–|isbn=978-1-4047-5113-2}}</ref>
*  1779 &ndash; [[Zebulon Pike]], American general and explorer (died 1813)<ref>{{cite book|title=Somerset County Historical Quarterly|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wg1JAQAAMAAJ|year=1919|publisher=Somerset County Historical Society|page=241}}</ref>
*[[1781]] &ndash; [[Gaspar Flores de Abrego]], three terms mayor of San Antonio, in Spanish Texas (died 1836)<ref name="JYL">{{cite news|author=Camilla Campbell|date=November 26, 2008|url=http://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/online/articles/ffl26|title=Handbook of Texas Online: FLORES DE ABREGO, JOSÉ GASPAR MARÍA|publisher= Handbook of Texas Online}} Consulted in May 22–26, 2010.</ref>
*[[1793]] &ndash; [[Harvey Putnam]], American lawyer and politician (died 1855)<ref>{{cite book|author=James Osborne Putnam|title=Biographical Sketch of the Late Hon. Harvey Putnam|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RxwuAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA5|year=1868|publisher=Haas & Kelley|page=5}}</ref>
*[[1808]] &ndash; [[Anton Füster]], Austrian priest and activist (died 1881)<ref>{{cite book|title=Acta neophilologica|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZRfzAAAAMAAJ|year=1998|publisher=Filozofska fakulteta Univerze v Ljubljani|page=83}}</ref>
